en.headline: Customs and police raid 23 Sham Shui Po cigarette spots
en.dek: A joint operation from 18 to 30 September seized about 100,000 illicit cigarettes worth an estimated HK$480,000 and led to five arrests.
body: Customs and Sham Shui Po police broke up a series of illicit-cigarette cases in the district between 18 and 30 September, seizing about 100,000 cigarettes with an estimated street value of HK$480,000 and a dutiable value of about HK$350,000, according to reports on Monday evening that cited the enforcement figures.
Officers raided 22 temporary storage points and one mobile stall. Five people were arrested: two local men, two local women and a Vietnamese man.

Customs said it would keep using several tactics against the trade. Under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance, handling, possessing, selling or buying illicit cigarettes is an offence, and the maximum penalty on conviction is a fine of HK$2 million and seven years in prison.
The department asked the public to report suspected cases on its 24-hour hotline.

zh.headline: 海關聯同深水埗警區搞破23個私煙據點
zh.dek: 9月18日至30日的聯合行動檢獲約10萬支私煙，估計市值48萬元，拘捕五人，包括四名本地人士及一名越南籍男子。
body: 海關與深水埗警區在9月18日至30日在區內偵破多宗私煙案。星期一晚間的報道引述行動數字，指檢獲約10萬支私煙，估計市值48萬元，應課稅值約35萬元。
人員搞破22個臨時儲藏點和一個流動檔攤，拘捕兩名本地男子、兩名本地女子和一名越南籍男子。
海關表示會繼續多管齊下打擊私煙。根據《應課稅品條例》，處理、管有、售賣或購買私煙均屬違法，一經定罪最高可被罰款200萬元及監禁七年。
海關呼籲市民如懷疑有私煙活動，可致電24小時熱線舉報。
